uncited: Rendering Pipeline Architecture refers to the structural organization of hardware-accelerated splatting techniques, where volumetric or point-cloud data is decomposed into primitives (splats) and rasterized to form an image [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

It solves the problem of efficiently rendering large-scale volumetric datasets in real-time by leveraging GPU rasterization pipelines for transformation, projection, and compositing [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

It differs from ray-marching methods by using screen-space accumulation (compositing along sheets) rather than per-ray sampling, and from single-pass mesh rendering by explicitly handling transparency and depth occlusion through multi-stage or specialized accumulation buffers [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
The splatting family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].
**Primitive Representation:** The volume is decomposed into primitives.
These may be explicit geometric shapes (cubes, cells, splats) or implicit functions sampled via texture hardware [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1, unofficial][S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
**Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., shear-warp) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial].
For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., EWA splatting) to account for foreshortening [S6, unofficial][S10, abstract only, unofficial].
**Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane.
This step leverages hardware-accelerated scan-conversion, depth testing, and blending [S1, S2, S3, S4, unofficial].

**Compositing:** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image.
This is typically done using alpha blending in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, S2, S3, unofficial][S7].
Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, abstract only, unofficial].
**Hardware Acceleration:** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].
The concept of splatting was introduced by Levoy [S1, unofficial] as a method for volume visualization.
The family evolved to address the limitations of early software-based rendering by leveraging GPU hardware acceleration [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

Subsequent developments focused on improving attribute quality [1066-splat-attributes-pass.md], reducing pass counts [1254-single-pass-splat-rendering-pipeline.md], and ensuring numerical correctness in perspective projection [2837-three-pass-gpu-point-rendering-pipeline.md].
